2.text: the other priests and missionaries led him to act very strangely at times.

3.text: Thus he would pay no attention to religious ceremonials performed by other

4.text: priests, and would perform the church marriage-ritual for a Chukchee man

6.text: After the affair of the kettle, Father Venedict suddenly resolved to make

7.text: good his promise to the bishop, and he actually went away with some Reindeer

8.text: Chukchee who were going toward East Cape. He travelled about two years,

9.text: and visited all the Chukchee villages along the coasts of both oceans. Of

10.text: course, he had to suffer many hardships. All his provisions were exhausted,

11.text: and during the last part of his journey he lived completely the life of the

12.text: natives. I met him on the Wolverene River, when he had fairly started on

13.text: his voyage. This was in the spring of 1897.

14.text: While on another journey through the Chukchee villages on the Pacific

15.text: shore, three years afterwards, Kɪlaˊtɪ, a Chukchee in the village of Valkaˊʟ̣ên,

16.text: gave me some interesting details about his return to the Anadyr. Father

17.text: Venedict went to see Kɪlaˊtɪ with some Maritime Chukchee, and staid with

18.text: him for eighteen days. Before that he had lived some days in the American

19.text: log-cabin on St. Lawrence Bay. The Americans were acting as agents of

20.text: the American Government for buying reindeer. Mr. I. Kelly was one of them.

21.text: They showed much kindness to the travelling priest, gave him some provisions,

22.text: a rifle, a knife, a hatchet, etc. Kɪlaˊtɪ related the story thus: —

23.text: “Our place is not very windy; but farther on to the south, halfway to the village Rêˊtkên,

24.text: near the river Iruˊ-veˊem, the wind blows all the time: so it was impossible to go there. We told

25.text: him so. He would not believe us, and, after a few days of waiting, left on foot, quite alone, and

26.text: without provisions. He was much afraid to stay with our people for another winter. We said to

27.text: him, ‘The Russian settlement is not far, you will have time to reach there;’ but he thought we

28.text: were deceiving him, so he left on foot along the shore. I caught him, however, and brought him

29.text: back. He left again, and this time gained quite a little headway. The wind was cutting; but I

30.text: harnessed my team and went in pursuit. After some time I saw him on the shore. Then I stopped

31.text: my dogs, and began to steal along towards him as one steals up to a wild reindeer, because he was

32.text: greatly agitated, and I was afraid that he would run away. Then all of a sudden I stepped out in

33.text: front of him. Then I said, ‘Now, do come back! You see it is impossible to go. We have no

34.text: chiefs or authorities. So, if the wind should blow you into the sea, your people would not believe

35.text: it. They would say that we killed you. It would be a bad thing, a great calamity, and interrupt

36.text: the traffic.’ He said nothing, but lay down on the ground and turned away from me. All at once

37.text: a white fox jumped out from the stones. The dogs followed. I caught hold of the sledge, but was

38.text: unable to stop it: so I tried at least to direct it properly; but we were so near to the brink, that

39.text: I expected every minute to fall into the water. At last I succeeded in stopping the dogs. The

40.text: water was as if boiling underneath. I felt very angry, and said to the priest, ‘See, now! For your

41.text: sake I nearly lost my life by being drowned in the water. Sit down on the sledge! Otherwise I

42.text: shall bind you.’ So I brought him back. In a week after that the wind subsided. Then I said,

43.text: ‘Now let us go!’ So we went, and reached Mariinsky Post.”

44.text: At Mariinsky Post, Kɪlaˊtɪ was rewarded with some tea and tobacco. Father

45.text: Venedict himself had no shirt on, and his fur clothes were full of insects.

46.text: He proceeded to Markova, and thence to Kolyma. On this last journey he

47.text: again had bad luck. He and his companions lost their way in the snow, and
